Kuvitus: astronautti Kuun harmaalla pinn: Illustration: an astronaut on the grey surface of the Moon against a black sky, with the lunar module behind and the Earth in the sky. The astronaut has dropped a hammer and a feather at the same time; faint in-between images show that they are at the same height at every moment and that the gaps between the images grow during the fall.
(t,v)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vapaasti pu: (t,v) graph to scale: the speed of a freely falling object is a straight line starting from the origin. The points are 9.81 m/s at 1.0 s, 19.6 m/s at 2.0 s, 29.4 m/s at 3.0 s and 39.2 m/s at 4.0 s. Between the moments 1.0 s and 3.0 s the time increases by 2.0 s and the speed by 19.6 m/s, so the slope of the line is 9.81 m/s², the acceleration of free fall g.
(t,v)-kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kaksi suora: (t,v) graph to scale: two straight lines from the origin, showing the speed v as a function of time t of a body dropped from rest on the surface of planet A and of planet B. The grid spacing is 1 s and 5 m/s. The line of planet A passes through the grid crossing (5 s; 20 m/s) and the line of planet B through the crossing (5 s; 40 m/s). The time axis extends to 6 seconds.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa: pallo putoaa le: Diagram to scale: a ball falls from rest beside a measuring rod, and its positions are drawn at 0, 1, 2 and 3 seconds. The fall distances are 0, 4.9, 19.6 and 44.1 metres, and the gaps between successive positions, 4.9, 14.7 and 24.5 metres, grow. The arrow below the ball shows its velocity, and its length is proportional to the speed: 0, 9.81, 19.6 and 29.4 metres per second, so the speed grows by the same amount every second.
Kaavakuva: kaksi teräspalloa, 1 kg ja 5: Diagram: two steel balls, 1 kg and 5 kg, fall from rest at the same time without air resistance; the heavier ball is larger. At every moment, 0, 1 and 2 seconds, the balls are at the same height and their velocity arrows are equally long: 0, 9.81 and 19.6 metres per second. A dashed line passes through the tips of both arrows.
Kuvitus: omenapuun oksasta irronnut omen: Illustration: an apple that has come off a branch of an apple tree falls towards the grass. The branch has leaves and another apple; above the falling apple a dashed circle marks the place it came off.
Kaavakuva: telineessä on kaksi valoportt: Diagram: a stand holds two light gates, one below the other. In each gate light travels from a transmitter to a receiver. At the top a clamp holds a 5.0 cm long body, which is dropped from rest through the gates. The gates are connected to a timer that measures how long the light is cut off in each gate.
